channel.title: Wire — Go
channel.description: Go from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: The Data Race That Wasn't a Bug (and the One That Was)
item.description: You turn on Go’s race detector and get a data race inside net/http that makes no sense at first. (1 source: golangweekly)

item.title: Nail Your Complex Go Backend
item.description: Get started with Domain-Driven Design in Go with real-world projects, best practices, and proven patterns. Avoid common pitfalls. Created by the trusted authors of the Three Dots Labs blog and Watermill library. (1 source: golangweekly)

item.title: A Terminal Protocol for Program Status (OSC 7501)
Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6
item.description: Go maintainers declined netip.Addr.Map() saying the compiler should optimize netip.AddrFrom16(ip.As16()) instead. How difficult is it to implement? (2 sources: golangweekly, lobsters)

item.title: Hooking into the Go Toolchain
item.description: How go build -toolexec lets us time, rewrite and instrument every compiler and linker run, from a small stopwatch to OpenTelemetry's otelc. (1 source: golangweekly)

item.title: a compiler bug that could corrupt values
Every Go release since 2013, benchmarked
item.description: We measured the fastest Benchmarks Game Go programs on each Go release since 1.2. Go 1.27 is 11.5% faster than Go 1.23. Most of the recent improvement comes from the runtime. (1 source: golangweekly)
